lane_impact: L2 skills-meters / L5 combat-core: corrects the Focus contract before it ships. FOCUS_REGEN = +6 per kill event (clamped to max), NOT per tick. Do not write '+6/tick' into config. Also record the web/android HUD zero-point divergence (48 vs 24) so the third bar is not ported from the android formula.
text: The Focus finding in this packet ships 'regen +6/tick' in its lane_impact. That trigger was never opened, and it is wrong. bonusReload() has exactly one caller in the whole android bundle: NPCManager.as:1709-1711, inside the sweep at :1695-1706 that walks the enemy list, calls checkDie() on each, and counts deaths — so the +6 fires once per frame in which at least one enemy DIED, not once per frame. Focus is a kill-fed resource. That is also why the frames make sense: at Nr4fQstqHDM_428.0 the bar sits at zero mid-fight, and by t435.0s, after kills, it is ~40% full. A per-tick trickle would never sit empty through an active fight. Note the build divergence in the same function while I was there: android :3272 pushes '(this.reload - 24) / (this.maxreload - 24)' to the HUD, while web §1t113s0§.as:328 computes '(param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48)' inside the HUD from raw values — so the bar's zero point is 24 on android and 48 on web. Only on WEB does the empty bar coincide exactly with the stance gate at 48, which is precisely why the web build can afford to use the empty bar as the 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' readout and android carries no such label.

quote: web §1t99s0§.as:3060 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48)' vs android MCSPlayer.as:2977 'if(this.reload < this.maxreload / 6)' · web §1t113s0§.as:328 '(param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48)' vs android MCSPlayer.as:3272 'updateReload((this.reload - 24) / (this.maxreload - 24))'
text: S0-3's parity caveat says UI copy and combat tuning parity between web v0.717 and android v0.682 is NOT established. Judging this packet measured four concrete divergences, all in COMBAT TUNING rather than copy, which discharges the caveat's 'not established' into 'established, and they differ'. (1) SPD->cooldown cap: 600 on web, 300 on android — the mobile build halves cooldowns at half the stat. (2) In-combat stance gate: a flat 'reload < 48' on web, 'reload < maxreload / 6' on android — which is 8 + SPD, so the two only agree at SPD 40. (3) HUD reload zero point: 48 on web, 24 on android; only the web build's empty bar coincides with its stance gate, which is why only the web build can use the empty bar as the 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' readout and android's BattleUI carries no such label. (4) Per-stance reach multipliers: web 1.4 / 1 + 0.02m / 0.5 + 0.04m against android 1.5 / 1 + 0.005M / 0.5 + 0.005M. In every one of the four the web value is the one a v0.717 recreation must take, and in every one an agent porting the android row would have shipped a wrong number that no test would catch. Corollary for this lane's own rules: a claim resting on an android combat constant while asserting web behaviour is not a theoretical parity hole — it is wrong four times out of four in the region I sampled.

text: Two things at once. (1) RR:195 skills-meters blocker (2) correctly denies that spacebar is slow-motion in Duels ('spacebar-slowmo belongs to the predecessor SHS2'); the positive answer is now known. §1t1541s0§.as:603-616: 'case Keyboard.SPACE:' takes the player, and 'if(!§1t10074s0§ && _loc2_.§1t4470s0§())' runs '_loc2_.§1t4472s0§();' plus Snd_smallClick, else Snd_error. SPACE cycles stance through the same 48-Focus gate as the HUD button. (2) A correction to SHSD_MASTER_REFERENCE.md:387, which grades as [CONTRACT] that out of combat stance change is an 'Instant toggle, no cooldown, no cost (SPACE or portrait click)'. Those are TWO different code paths and only one is unconditional. The portrait-click path (§1t406s0§.as:3064-3104) has no meter test at all. The SPACE path runs §1t4470s0§()/§1t4472s0§(), and §1t4472s0§ re-guards unconditionally at §1t99s0§.as:3060 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48){ return; }' - that guard is NOT wrapped in the in-battle test, unlike the -48 debit at :3160-3166. So out of combat SPACE is free but still REQUIRES 48 Focus, while the portrait click is free and unconditional. PARTIAL because I have not established §1t1541s0§'s key handler is live outside battle - it checks text-focus against BOTH §1t113s0§.instance (BattleUI) and §1t406s0§.instance (overworld) at :595-602, which suggests a global handler, but that is an inference and I am not grading it as proved.

lane_impact: Discharges the S0-3 caveat's warning with a concrete example instead of a worry: combat tuning demonstrably diverges between v0.682 and v0.717 even where the data XMLs match. Any lane porting a combat number must name the build.
text: A first-hand, non-circular measurement of the S0-3 build-parity hole, on the exact system this packet is about. WEB v0.717: maxreload = 8*24 = 192 (§1t99s0§.as:249), stance threshold 48 (§1t99s0§.as:3050,:3060), HUD normalisation (v-48)/(max-48) (§1t113s0§.as:328) - threshold and HUD zero-point agree, and 48/192 is exactly one quarter. ANDROID v0.682: maxreload = 5*24 = 120 (MCSPlayer.as:239), HUD normalisation (reload-24)/(maxreload-24) (MCSPlayer.as:1163-1168), and nextStance gates at 'if(this.reload < this.maxreload / 6) return;' = 20 (MCSPlayer.as:2977) - so Android's gate (20) and its HUD zero-point (24) do not even agree with each other. The web build did not merely renumber: it raised the ceiling 120 -> 192, doubled the threshold 24 -> 48, and repaired the gate/HUD mismatch. Every Focus, crit and stance-cost number therefore has to be read from the web payload; none may be ported from Android. Same conclusion from the crit branch: web is a flat *1.3 for all stances (§1t99s0§.as:3274) while Android is *1.2 for non-Light and *1.5 for Light (MCSPlayer.as:3219-3221).

SPD's real reach into the meter is zero; SPD buys reach (120 + floor((90+DAN*5)*spd/(20+spd))) and skill cooldown (1 - min(spd,600)/600*0.5), and that is all. quote: MCSPlayer.as:105 'internal var baseReload:int = 48;' ‖ MCSPlayer.as:190 'this.baseReload = baseReload;' ‖ MCSPlayer.as:239 'this.maxreload = 5 * 24;' ‖ §1t99s0§.as:249 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;'
text: The single fact that decides the Focus-capacity dispute, stated positively so no future packet re-derives it wrong: 48 + (SPD + gearSPD) * 6 is baseReload, NOT maxreload, and it is dead code in BOTH builds. Android MCSPlayer.as contains exactly three occurrences of the identifier 'baseReload' - the field declaration at :105 ('internal var baseReload:int = 48;'), the initPlayer parameter at :182, and the assignment at :190 ('this.baseReload = baseReload;'). Nothing ever reads it. maxreload is a separate field assigned flat: 5*24 = 120 in android (MCSPlayer.as:239), 8*24 = 192 in web (§1t99s0§.as:249). The web side is the same shape - §1t1523s0§.as:2268 passes §1t9588s0§() as the 7th argument into §1t4443s0§ (the 15-arg initPlayer twin at §1t99s0§.as:183), and the only assignments to §1t4415s0§ anywhere in the bundle are the two flat 8*24 lines. Because the field is dead in BOTH builds, C2 does not apply: this is not a v0.682-vs-v0.717 divergence, it is a field mix-up, and any finding that reports 48+SPD*6 as the Focus maximum is wrong regardless of which build it claims.

text: An independent arithmetic corroboration of the 6x6 rule that costs nothing and closes a loop between two findings banked from unrelated artifacts. I counted the territory bitmap myself: reference/extracted/android/110_Mobile_MapBitmapData.bin decodes as a 63x72 GIF in palette mode with exactly 735 lit pixels (PIL, threshold >127 on the L conversion), one per existing territory — matching the banked world-map finding. This is the kind of check a per-claim lens cannot run, and it means the world's node count is a DERIVED quantity a rebuild can assert, not a measured one.

lane_impact: L5 combat-core: the reach pipeline is baseSlashLength x (debuff 0.5?) x stanceMult, floored at 100 for Heavy — and the same debuff halves ATK and DEF. Add the branch to the stance/reach config.
text: Unclaimed, and it changes the reach model's shape. §1t99s0§.as:219-224 is a third branch of the same buff switch that grants minDamage x1.5 (:213) and defense x1.5 (:217): 'else if(§1t1523s0§.§1t9725s0§(§1t1523s0§.§1t9463s0§)) { this.minDamage *= 0.5; this.defense *= 0.5; this.§1t4420s0§ *= 0.5; }'. §1t4420s0§ is baseSlashLength, so a live debuff HALVES reach at the base, before the stance multiplier and before the Heavy floor of 100 — meaning under this state Light runs 84-147 px and Heavy is pinned at its 100 floor for every speed value. The constants: §1t1523s0§.as:328/330/332 give buff ids 1 (ATK), 2 (DEF), 3 (SPD), and :348 'internal static const §1t9463s0§:int = 11;' is the debuff, checked on its OWN timer slot at :5011-5017 ('if(param1 == §1t9463s0§) return §1t7356s0§(§1t9433s0§) > ...') rather than the shared buff slot the other three use — i.e. a curse can run concurrently with a buff. Every reach finding in the corpus models base -> stance -> floor with no debuff term.

lane_impact: L4 progression: ship STAT_CAP_{ATK,DEF,SPD} = 1 + (level+10)*3 with a STRICT '<' grant gate, base 1 step 3, budget (level-1)*3. Strike the 'unreachable in one stat' clause from s26c/the-271-cap-IS-the-shipped-level-80-base-stat-cap.
text: The reason s26c/the-271-cap-IS-the-shipped-level-80-base-stat-cap and progression/271-cap-explained disagree is a single comparison operator, and it is on the page. §1t5957s0§.as:3344 gates the ATK add-button on 'stat < 1 + (_loc2_ + 10) * 3' — a STRICT less-than — and :3422 grants exactly +3. Base ATK is 1 (§1t1523s0§.as:2567 sets §1t9408s0§ to 1 on stat reset; :3457 audits spend as (ATK - 1) / 3, which independently pins base 1 step 3). The reachable set is therefore {1, 4, 7, ..., 268, 271}, and 271 = 1 + 3*90 is ON the lattice: at 268 the gate is still open, the grant fires, ATK becomes 271, and only then does the button hide. 'Unreachable because the panel stops granting' inverts what the operator does — a strict '<' hides the button AFTER the cap is reached, not before. The budget half is not close either: §1t1523s0§.as:2577 sets the pool to (getLevel() - 1) * 3 = 237 at the level cap of 80 (:362 'public static const §1t9470s0§:int = 80;'), against a 90-point cost. Bank the operator, not just the formula: a rebuild that ships '<=' produces a 274 cap.

An equality test IS the answer: it is deterministic. §1t99s0§.as:3255-3277 is the whole outgoing-damage routine and the only RNG in it is the base-damage roll; the crit arm at :3272-3274 is gated purely on reload == maxreload, and :3295-3297 then zeroes a full meter, so the crit both fires on and consumes the full bar.
